title: Sectionwise log unit conditions imply the geometric-stalk log conditions
statement: Let X be a scheme with small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and M an etale prelog structure [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], consisting of a sheaf of commutative monoids and a natural homomorphism alpha to the multiplicative structure ring sheaf. Suppose for every etale V and section s of M(V), invertibility of alpha(s) implies invertibility of s, and the induced map M(V)^times -> Gamma(V,O_V)^times is bijective. Then the same prelog structure admits the structure of an EtaleLogStructure: at every geometric point, its structural stalk homomorphism reflects units and is bijective on unit groups. The stalks are the pointed-etale filtered colimits [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. No local Noetherian, integrality, cancellation or finiteness assumption is needed.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1, printed p.69 (PDF p.75), etale log conventions; agent-supplied associated-log quotient and stalk calculation, since the cited Kato (1988), section 1, is unavailable. The section-to-geometric-stalk passage at the end of Step 5 of lem-trf-prelog-pushout-log-axiom.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point. The opposite category of pointed etale neighbourhoods is filtered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]. The monoid stalk and ring stalk are the colimits of the respective section diagrams [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Their underlying sets are colimits: use preservation of filtered colimits by the forgetful functors for commutative monoids and commutative rings [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-filtered-colimit-underlying], [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]. The stalk structure map commutes with the cocone maps by the colimit-desc equations.

proof.text: In any filtered diagram of commutative monoids whose underlying sets have the stated colimit, a section whose colimit image is a unit becomes a unit after restriction. Represent an inverse in some stage, pass to a common stage, and refine until the product equals one using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]. Commutativity makes this one product equation sufficient.

proof.text: Represent a monoid stalk element by a section. If its structural image is invertible, the previous step applied to the ring section diagram makes the structural image of the restricted section invertible. The assumed sectionwise reflection makes the monoid section a unit. Its image in the stalk is the original element, proving reflection.

proof.text: For surjectivity on stalk units, represent a ring unit, refine until its representative is a unit by the second step, and lift it using sectionwise surjectivity of the units map. Its monoid germ is the required preimage. For injectivity, represent the values of two monoid units in a common stage. Refine until both representatives are units, and then refine until their structural images agree, using the equality criterion for filtered colimits. Sectionwise injectivity on units gives equality of their values there, hence equality of their germs and of the stalk units. These two conclusions are exactly the extra fields of EtaleLogStructure, retaining the given prelog structure unchanged.

theorem etale_log_of_section_units {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : EtalePrelogStructure X)
    (hreflect : ∀ (V : X.Etaleᵒᵖ) (s : M.monoidSheaf.obj.obj V),
      IsUnit (M.alpha.app V s) → IsUnit s)
    (hbij : ∀ V : X.Etaleᵒᵖ, Function.Bijective (Units.map (M.alpha.app V).hom)) :
    ∃ Λ : EtaleLogStructure X, Λ.toEtalePrelogStructure = M
